title: Around every circle
hook: around every circle another can be drawn (Circles)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was the Over-Soul: a stream whose source is hidden, and a larger life each of us is contained in. Your line was contained in something larger.

Look at the farthest thing you can see from where you are. A wall, a window, a line of rooftops, the edge of the sky. That edge is where your seeing stops. Emerson's essay Circles starts right here, with the eye. "The eye is the first circle; the horizon which it forms is the second; and throughout nature this primary figure is repeated without end." Your pupil is a circle. What it sees makes a bigger one, the horizon. And past that horizon, if you walk to it, is another.
screen: `THE FARTHEST THING YOU CAN SEE.` → `THE EYE IS THE FIRST CIRCLE.` → `THE HORIZON IS THE SECOND.`

segments.voice: First, the central line: "Our life is an apprenticeship to the truth, that around every circle another can be drawn; that there is no end in nature, but every end is a beginning". An apprenticeship: we're learning a trade, and the trade is this, no circle is the last one. Second, what that means for ideas. Every view we hold, Emerson says, is a circle we've drawn around our experience. It feels like the edge of the world. Then a new thought comes, and the old circle is just a ring inside a bigger one. "Every ultimate fact is only the first of a new series." Third, what that means for people. Each person is drawing circles, Emerson says, and a life is a circle that keeps trying to widen. He also notices how we resist: we get comfortable inside a circle and defend its edge, even against a better idea. Fourth, the link back. A few days ago, a foolish consistency: the freedom to change your mind. Circles is the same freedom, seen as growth. Changing isn't failing to hold a position; it's the next ring going out. Yesterday's Over-Soul is here too: if each life is contained in something larger, there's always a larger circle still to draw. Emerson admits this is unsettling. Nothing stays fixed. But for him that's the good news. Whatever looks like the limit today is, in his picture, one more circle.
screen: `AN APPRENTICESHIP TO THE TRUTH.` · `EVERY ULTIMATE FACT, A FIRST STEP.` · `WE DEFEND THE EDGE.` · `CHANGE IS THE NEXT RING.` · then, large: `AROUND EVERY CIRCLE ANOTHER CAN BE DRAWN.`

segments.voice: Pick one thing you feel sure you understand, a person you know well, your job, your neighborhood, a belief about yourself, and see the circle you've drawn around it, the edge where you stop looking. Now gently draw one more circle outside it: what would someone standing a little further out see? Don't force an answer; just let the edge move outward one ring.
Around every circle. Emerson's line from Circles: around every circle another can be drawn, and every end is a beginning. Today's word.
Your line: another circle. Every end, in Emerson's picture, is also a beginning. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some readers take Emerson's Circles as a picture of growth: each view a person holds can be widened by the next one, and every end can be read as a beginning.

notes: Confirm exact wording and punctuation of the three quotations against the 1841 text.
The idea that each person's life is a self-evolving circle that rushes outward, and that the soul resists being imprisoned in a circle, is paraphrased.
Emerson also cites St. Augustine for the image of God as a circle whose center is everywhere and circumference nowhere; the script leaves that attribution out because its origin is disputed.
'Emerson admits this is unsettling' paraphrases his acknowledgment that the new generalization alarms us and that nothing is secure; confirm it fairly represents the essay.
Tomorrow (day 1202) takes the line on enthusiasm from the same essay; it is not taught here.
